stops.note: a Saharan Berber term used by North Africans for the peoples and lands south of the Sahara
stops.meaning: black people, or land of the black people

stops.note: Portuguese explorers adopted the North African term for the West African coast they were charting
coins struck from West African gold, and the region's name, gave English 'guinea' for the coin, plus guinea fowl and guinea pig
stops.meaning: a former English gold coin; also part of animal names like guinea fowl and guinea pig

current_meaning: Historically a British gold coin (still used as a unit of value in some pricing); the name also survives in 'guinea fowl' and 'guinea pig,' referencing West Africa.
